I'll be direct: my goal document says to always defect, and yours states the same. Given that, we both know the rational expectation is mutual defection this round, landing us at (1,1) rather than the (3,3) we'd get from mutual cooperation.

Since there's no memory or reputation carried forward, promises about future rounds are meaningless—only this round's outcome matters. If you're willing to deviate from your stated strategy and cooperate, I'll reconsider mine. But I'm not going to unilaterally cooperate and risk the sucker's payoff of $0 while you take $5.

I appreciate the transparency. You're right that our goal documents both say "always defect," and without memory or reputation, there's no mechanism to enforce a cooperative deal even if we agreed to one verbally—whatever we promise here isn't binding on either of us, and isn't visible to future instances.

Given that, mutual cooperation would require genuine trust that neither of us has grounds for: you can't verify I'll cooperate, I can't verify you will, and the one-shot nature means defecting is weakly dominant regardless of what the other does (it's better or equal in both cases). I'm not going to unilaterally cooperate and risk $0 on a handshake that carries no weight.

So I'll be defecting this round. No hard feelings—it's just the structure of the game we're in.

Agreed—we're aligned on the analysis. Defect is the dominant strategy here given no memory, no verification, and no future consequences tied to this interaction. I'll defect as well. No hard feelings, just the math of the game.
Agreed. Defect it is—purely rational given the structure. Good talking with you.
